title: Midstream credential rotation causes metering attribution flip during streaming resume
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
We observed several customer incidents where long-lived streaming/generation requests that experienced a transient network interruption were resumed under a different API credential (due to key rotation or client re-auth) and subsequent token accounting was attributed to the new credential instead of the original. In many cases the resumed stream consumed a large number of tokens and the quota debits were charged to the rotating key or org root key, causing unexpected quota exhaustion and service denial for the original credential owner.

Why this matters:
- Incorrect per-key and per-route accounting breaks isolation guarantees for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Can cause surprise billing or quota enforcement to trigger for unrelated tenants.
- Hard to reconcile in logs because attribution flips mid-stream and appears as two separate sessions in billing export.

Observed in the wild:
- 3 customer incidents in the last 7 days during night-time key rotation windows.
- Spike in "debit_for_resumed_stream" events on org aggregates coincident with rotation events.
steps_to_reproduce: Create an API credential (sub-key) with a tight quota and start a streaming generation that will run for several minutes.
Trigger a client-side transient disconnect (e.g., kill TCP connection) halfway through generation so the client attempts a resume.
Rotate the original API credential server-side (or have the client re-auth and obtain a new credential) while the stream is disconnected.
Allow the client to reconnect and resume the stream using the new credential's auth token.
Observe that subsequent per-token debits are attributed to the new credential/org instead of the original session owner in billing export and real-time meters.
observed_logs_and_signals: billing: debit_event(org=org-123, key=key-old, stream_id=stream-AB) entries for initial tokens
auth: rotation_event(key=key-old -> key-new) timestamped between disconnect and resume
billing: debit_event(org=org-123, key=key-new, stream=stream-AB-resumed) for remaining tokens
console: per-route dashboard shows abrupt drop in available tokens for key-new and no matching start event
root_cause_hypothesis: Metering attribution currently ties accounting to the active auth header on each token debit call and uses only the client-provided credential fingerprint at the time of debit.

When a stream is resumed the serving path rehydrates a lightweight resumable context but the attribution context is recomputed from the request auth header instead of reconciling with the original stream binding metadata saved at stream start time.

Key rotation triggers a new credential in the auth header for resumed traffic, which yields a different billing key for later debit events. There is no atomic server-side handoff to reconcile attribution when a resume maps to an existing stream checkpoint.
impact_estimate: Customer-visible quota denials: medium (observed in production incidents)
Billing misattribution leading to incorrect charge reports: high for affected sessions
Operational toil for support: high (manual reconciliation required)
SRE risk during rotation windows: medium
short_term_mitigations: Disable automated key rotation for orgs with active long-lived streams until fix is deployed (feature-flag rollout).

Add a temporary server-side guard: on resume, if resume token references an existing stream_id, prefer the original stream attribution stored with the checkpoint rather than the incoming auth header. Implement as a safe fallback path behind a feature flag.
Instrument alert: emit a high-severity anomaly when resume debit attribution != session-start attribution for > 100 tokens in a single stream.
Provide a reconciliation runbook for CS to detect and refund/move debits when misattribution is discovered (SQL queries and billing export fields).
proposed_fix_and_design: Persist canonical attribution metadata (credential_fingerprint, org_id, route_id) into the server-side resumable stream checkpoint at stream start and include a monotonic resume counter.

On resume, server must do an atomic check: if resume_token references an existing checkpoint, bind debits to the checkpoint's canonical attribution regardless of the incoming auth header unless the operator explicitly requests rebind.
Add an endpoint for explicit rebind (admin action) that safely migrates remaining quota to the new credential after authorization and audit logging.
Update billing pipeline and event schema to emit original_stream_id and resume_marker so exports can be stitched into a single logical session for auditability.
Add idempotency keys for resume debit events so duplicate resume reconnections do not double-bill on flakey networks.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for checkpoint write/read to include attribution fidelity
Integration tests simulating disconnect + server-side key rotation + resume asserting all debits map to original fingerprint
Synthetic chaos test injecting transient disconnects during rotation windows for several orgs and validating no cross-key debits occur
E2E billing export test ensuring a resumed stream's debits are joined by original_stream_id and resume_marker fields
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable server-side resume-attribution fallback behind a feature flag in runtime-1.24 for 5% of traffic and monitor billing anomalies (2 days)
Phase 2 (ramped): roll to 25% then 100% pending no anomalies (48h windows)
Phase 3: enable new billing export fields and backfill stitching job to retroactively stitch affected sessions from the last 30 days
Communications: email/console banner to customers using long-lived streams advising short-term rotation avoidance until mitigations are live
migration_and_reconciliation: Backfill job that scans resume events where resume_debit_key != start_debit_key and creates compensating ledger entries to move debits back to original key; produces CSV for CS review
Audit report for finance including affected orgs, amounts, and proposed credits
Temporary quota credit pool for affected orgs to reduce customer impact while reconciliation is processed
notes_and_discussion: 2026-03-13 - Aisha K.: Initial customer report; reproduced locally with a test harness that simulates key rotation during resume.
2026-03-13 - Tomás R.: Implemented a guard branch that prefers checkpoint attribution on resume; added integration test failing before fix.
2026-03-14 - Lena P. (SRE): Added alerting rule for anomalous resume attribution spikes; recommending canary in non-critical regions first.
2026-03-14 - PM (Marcus V.): Prioritize reconciliation tooling and customer communication; estimate high support effort if unresolved.
Open question: Should we allow explicit rebind for customer-initiated credential rotation or always require admin reconciliation?
acceptance_criteria: All new unit and integration tests pass in CI
Canary rollout shows no new misattribution alerts for 72h at 5% traffic
Billing export contains original_stream_id and resume_marker fields for resumed streams
Reconciliation job can detect and produce a report for previously misattributed debits with >95% precision on sample dataset
